data.long_meaning: The name Sarfarz is a combination of two Persian words - Sar meaning 'king' and Farz meaning 'duty'. The name is a powerful one, suggesting someone who is a brave and valiant king, fulfilling his duties and leading his people with courage. The name Sarfarz carries the meaning “Valiant, Brave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Sarfarz usually hope their child will grow to embody valiant, brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The spiritual meaning of the name Sarfarz is that of a noble warrior, someone who is courageous in the face of adversity and dedicated to serving his community. It suggests a deep sense of responsibility and a strong moral compass.
data.etymology: Sarfarz belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Valiant, Brave.”

historical_references.reference: Sarfaraz Khan, a famous Mughal general in the late 16th century, served under Akbar. He was known for his valor and military skills. In 1576, he led the Mughal army to conquer Malwa and later, in 1583, he assisted Akbar in the Siege of Chittorgarh.

Sarfaraz Nawab, a powerful Pathan ruler in South India during the late 17th and early 18th centuries, ruled over the areas around Madurai. He was a vassal of the Nayak rulers of Thanjavur and expanded his territories through military conquests. In 1674, he successfully resisted the attempts of the Maratha forces to invade his lands.
